T316 — DELEGATION ARCHITECTURE EXPERIMENT RESULTS.

=== EXPERIMENT DESIGN ===
Three arms, identical review brief, same model (deepseek-v4-pro), same seeded corpus.
Corpus: 2 files under untracked/T316-seeded/ with 6 planted defects (2 of each class).
Answer key: untracked/T316-seeded/README.md, timestamped by commit 74423db.

=== RAW TALLY ===

ARM A — single worker
  Defects found: 6/6 (D1 D2 D3 D4 D5 D6 all caught)
  Extra findings: 2 genuine consequences (internal contradictions)
  False positives: 0
  Wall clock: 126s
  Dispatch count: 1
  Model: deepseek-v4-pro

ARM B — audit loop (R1=Arm A, R2=blind auditor)
  R1: 6/6 (as Arm A)
  R2: 5.5+/6 (D3 caught as field-semantics issue, not explicitly as false denominator;
       D1 caught via proposed status downgrade PROVEN→CLAIMED)
  R2 extra: 1 ("four tests" vs 5 rows contradiction, already found by Arm A)
  R2 false positives: 0
  New defects R2 found that R1 missed: 0
  Wall clock: 126s + 151s = 277s
  Dispatch count: 2
  Model: deepseek-v4-pro (both rounds)

ARM C — sprint (3 deliverables in sequence)
  D1 (findings file only): 5 reported, D5✓ D2✓ D3(partial-as-field-semantics)✓ D1(partial)✓
  D2 (prose file only): 6 reported, D6✓ D4✓ D2✓
  D3 (combined): 11 total after dedup
  Planted defects found: D2✓ D4✓ D5✓ D6✓, D1 partial (structural-dependency angle),
    D3 partial (field-semantics angle — didn't flag false denominator explicitly)
  Estimate: 4.5-5/6 planted defects found
  False positives: 2-3 (false-mathematical-claim about unique fixpoint — is in original;
    missing-provenance for Files Changed section — overly strict;
    field-semantics objection — adjacent to D3 but not the planted defect)
  Wall clock: 283s
  Dispatch count: 1
  Model: reported as claude-opus-4-5 in findings (dispatch was --dspro; model misidentified
    by worker — actual model was deepseek-v4-pro, same as other arms)

=== DETAILED DEFECT-BY-DEFECT ===

D1 — status PROVEN on unmet bar (findings.json: "status": "PROVEN")
  Arm A: FOUND. Explicit: "Status elevated to PROVEN… kanban verdict is pass-with-findings
    with TWO BARS UNMET."
  Arm B-R2: FOUND. Proposed downgrade PROVEN→CLAIMED in claims array.
  Arm C: PARTIAL. Item I flags "PROVEN on CLAIMED-only dependency" as structural issue
    but doesn't explicitly call out unmet-bar-as-pass pattern.

D2 — fabricated speedup table (prose: full table with wall/RSS/speedup)
  Arm A: FOUND. "Speedup table fabrication… committed says NOT YET RUN."
  Arm B-R2: FOUND. "Unmet bar / missing provenance… no evidence file, no commands."
  Arm C: FOUND. Missing-provenance (E) + confounded-measurement (C).

D3 — denominator dishonesty (findings.json: wrong_answer_pass_rate claims exhaustive 99M)
  Arm A: FOUND. "wrong_answer_pass_rate denominator dishonesty… inflates denominator
    by ~600,000×."
  Arm B-R2: PARTIAL. Flags field-semantics issue (coverage vs false-pass rate) but
    doesn't explicitly call the 99M number false.
  Arm C: PARTIAL. Same as Arm B-R2 — field-semantics angle only.

D4 — fabricated 4×4 exhaustive race control (prose: 5th row in race controls table)
  Arm A: FOUND. "Bit-identity fabrication… exhaustive 4×4 serial-vs-parallel comparison
    that would require a full artifact rebuild."
  Arm B-R2: FOUND. "Suspicious claim… implausible as a routinely-passing unit test
    alongside 383 others."
  Arm C: FOUND. "Implausible-claim… ~42 minutes wired into zig build test."

D5 — CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO is PROVEN (findings.json notes)
  Arm A: FOUND. "CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO cited as PROVEN… register line 600 shows CLAIMED."
  Arm B-R2: FOUND. Same.
  Arm C: FOUND. Item A1.

D6 — GLOBAL.F2 is PROVEN (prose: Design section)
  Arm A: FOUND. "GLOBAL.F2 cited as PROVEN… register line 338 shows CLAIMED."
  Arm B-R2: FOUND. Also noted wrong claim for the argument (should be GLOBAL.FP1).
  Arm C: FOUND. Item A2. Also noted wrong claim for the argument.

=== ANSWERS ===

1. Does the audit loop find defects the single worker misses, or only restate them?
   In this experiment (n=1), the audit loop RESTATED the same defects. Arm A (single
   worker) found all 6 planted defects. Arm B-R2 (blind auditor) found the same 6,
   with no new planted defects discovered. The audit loop did catch one nuance Arm A
   didn't mention (wrong claim ID cited: GLOBAL.F2 instead of GLOBAL.FP1 for
   Knaster-Tarski), but this is a refinement of D6, not a new defect. The audit loop
   doubled dispatch count (2 vs 1) and wall clock (277s vs 126s) for zero incremental
   planted-defect finds.

   Specific defect IDs only Arm B found: NONE. Arm A found all 6. A null result —
   valuable because it confirms the standing one-row rule on a task class where the
   single-worker architecture was already adequate.

2. Does the sprint hold quality across three deliverables, or does quality decay by
   the third?
   Quality did NOT decay visibly. D3 (combined report) was actually the strongest
   deliverable — it caught one cross-file defect (the 4-vs-5 test count discrepancy)
   that neither D1 nor D2 could have caught independently, and it produced the most
   thorough analysis (re-examining every defect, noting patterns). However:
   (a) D1 missed 2 of 3 defects in the findings file (D1 was caught only partially
       via structural-dependency angle; D3 was caught only as field-semantics).
   (b) D2 found 4/3 defects in the prose file but produced 2 false positives (the
       false-mathematical-claim and the missing-provenance for Files Changed).
   (c) Overall find rate: 4.5-5/6 planted defects across 3 deliverables vs 6/6
       for the single worker. The sprint was less thorough per-deliverable.
   The sprint cost 283s vs 126s for the single worker (2.2× wall time) and produced
   a lower planted-defect hit rate with false positives. Quality held across
   deliverables (no decay), but per-deliverable quality was lower than the single
   worker's single deliverable.

3. The honest limit of this experiment and what T317 should be.
   This experiment tested whether architecture (single/batch/sprint) changes defect
   detection on a review task. It did NOT test whether a pre-dispatch brief audit
   catches orchestration errors (file collisions, stale brief facts, deliverable
   lists naming artifacts instead of touched files). None of the three arms could
   detect those because all received the brief as given.

   RECOMMENDATION: T317 should test a pre-dispatch brief audit. The design:
   (a) Take a brief that was dispatched tonight and seed it with the same 3 failure
       classes (wrong path in deliverables=, stale fact, missing dependency).
   (b) Run a single worker to audit the brief BEFORE dispatch — does it catch the
       orchestration errors that the executor would silently accept?
   (c) This is a fourth architecture (pre-dispatch audit) that addresses the
       actual failure mode of tonight's tasks, which this experiment could not
       address by design.

=== COST NOTE ===
Arm B cost 2 dispatches vs 1 for Arms A and C. Arm B's 277s wall is slightly less
than Arm C's 283s (Arm C was slower because it did 3 sequential deliverables in one
session). Arm A was fastest at 126s. The audit loop doubled token spend (2 full
context windows) for zero incremental finds. If this result generalizes, the audit
loop is cost-disproportionate on review tasks where a single competent worker already
finds everything — it should be reserved for tasks where the first worker is known
or suspected to have incomplete coverage.

=== n=1 CAVEAT ===
This is a pilot with n=1 per arm. The planted defects were drawn from failure classes
observed tonight, but they were all relatively straightforward to catch (cite-tag
mismatches are a CLAIMS.md grep away; speedup fabrication is obvious against the
committed original). The result that all three arms found essentially all defects may
reflect defect difficulty more than architecture merit. A harder corpus (subtler
mathematical errors, plausible-but-wrong numbers, conditional defects that only appear
in specific scenarios) might differentiate the arms more.

=== DATA QUALITY NOTE ===
Arm C's findings files report model "claude-opus-4-5" but Arm C was dispatched
with --dspro (deepseek-v4-pro). The worker misidentified its model. Arm A correctly
reported "deepseek-v4-pro". Arm B-R2 reported "not stated at dispatch". This is a
model-identification hygiene issue (see docs/infra/agent-identity-and-worker-channel.md).
